DILG BAGONG "LIANAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph OPINION NO. S. JUL 08 2025 PAULO EBUEN EM Lot 15E Harold St., Kingsville Subd. Mambugan, Antipolo City Dear Mr. Em: This has reference to your letter dated February 12, 2025, requesting clarification on the applicability of Republic Act No. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act (DPA) to Government Employees' Employment Status. Particularly, you seek clarification of the following: l. Are government employees entitled to the same data privacy rights as private individuals under the DPA; 2. The names of these employees already appeared in the 2020 COA Covid Hazard Pay Report. Is the act of only confirming the present employment status such as positions, office/department, and salary grade of these individuals by the HRMO still covered by DPA; 3. Does the provision in Chapter I, Section 4 (a) (I and (b) of RA No. 10173, be considered an exception to the application of the DPA to government employees, particularly in cases involving public interest or transparency; 4. Is the DILG Opinion No. 91 s 2024 dated July 3, 2024 applicable in this matter; and 5. Does the act of Masinloc HRMO be considered a violation of section 5 (e) of RA 6713. The Data Privacy Act of 2012 is a piece of legislation by Congress aimed at protecting personal data of individuals and regulate personal information collected, used, stored and shared by both the public and private sectors. Section 4 of RA 10173 provides the scope of its applicability for processing all types of personal information to any natural and juridical persons involved in personal information processing. Nevertheless, it also provides an exception to wit: a) Information about any individual who is or was an officer or employee of a government institution that relates to the position or functions of an individual which includes: 1) The fact that the individual is or was an officer or employee of the government institution; 2) The title, business address and office telephone number "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

of the individual; 3) The classification, salary range and responsibilities of the position held by the individual; and 4) The name of the individual on a document prepared by the individual in the course of employment with the government. In response to your interrelated first, second and third queries, this Department holds the view that government employees are granted the same protection afforded to private individuals under the Data Protection Act, particularly when the information sought does not pertain to their official duties or current position. However, if the information merely concerns confirmation of the employee's present employment status, including their position and assigned office, or if the matter involves public interest and transparency, then such information falls outside the coverage of the Data Privacy Act. In such cases, the institution is duty-bound to disclose the requested information. With respect to the applicability of DILG Opinion No. 91 , Series of 2024, it bears emphasis that the said opinion pertains specifically to Job Order employees and the disclosure of their salaries as reflected in the COA Audit Report, including the list of consultants in the concerned LGU. It was not rendered for the purpose of filing complaints before the Office of the Ombudsman. Accordingly, the same is not applicable to the present matter. Finally, on the matter of Section 5 (e) of RA 6713, this Department maintains that the said provision pertains specifically to the principles of transparency and accountability with respect to documents related to governmental operations. This encompasses laws, regulations, contracts and other public documents that are maintained by government agencies. It explicitly states that public documents shall be accessible for inspection during reasonable working hours. While it appears that the Masinloc HRMO did not violate this provision, they are nonetheless obligated to act on your request for information, given the lawful and stated purposes of such request. This opinion is rendered based solely on the facts and representations disclosed in the letter and our appreciation thereof. For a more authoritative interpretation on issues concerning the scope and application of the Data Privacy Act, we respectfully suggest referring the matter to the National Privacy Commission. We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ROMEO . BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS-LLRALD/mag/kbm Page 2 of 2
